label: Liquefaction: how far the ground moves (0 where it does not liquefy)

inputs.name: pgv
inputs.description: PGV at the component, in cm/s: the shaking the occurrence model reads.

inputs.name: pga
inputs.description: PGA at the component, in g: below the model's floor the ground does not fail.

event_id.description: The scenario's USGS event id, whose magnitude (and rupture model) the function reads: the same map hazard.shakemap reads. The page sets it for every binding when an earthquake is chosen.

lateral_spread_within_km.description: Hazus lateral spread needs a free face: it applies only to stretches within this distance of water (the row's dw_km standing in for the distance to a free face); farther, the stretch only settles. Left out, lateral spread applies everywhere.

source.citation: Zhu, Baise & Thompson (2017) BSSA 107:1365, general model, as USGS gfail implements it (code.usgs.gov ghsc/esi/groundfailure, zhu_2017.py, commit fa7bd28). Given it occurs: Hazus 6.1 Technical Manual Sec. 4.2.2 lateral spreading and settlement, as OpenQuake implements them (github.com/gem/oq-engine openquake/sep/liquefaction, commit 0f9c75e).

description: PGD = 0 with probability 1 - P, P = P(liquefies) = 1 - (1 - f)^(L / patch), f = Zhu et al. (2017)'s areal coverage at x0 + b_pgv ln(min(PGV, clip) MSF(M)), MSF = 1 / (1 + exp(-2 (M - 6))), M the ShakeMap's magnitude, 0 below its PGV and PGA floors (patches of length 'patch' along the stretch taken as independent). Given it liquefies, PGD = the larger of the Hazus lateral spread, K_delta(M) a(PGA / PGA_t) inches (a = 12r - 12, 18r - 24, 70r - 180 over r = PGA / PGA_t in (1, 2], (2, 3], > 3; 0 for r <= 1), and the class's settlement: a fixed value given PGA. Where the model sets lateral_spread_within_km and the stretch is farther than that from water (dw_km), it has no free face and only settles. Occurrence is the event PGD > 0.
